source.title: HTTP Request with "Never Error" keeps returning 401 when a credential with an expiring token (preAuthentication) needs a refresh

source.body:
### Bug Description

Credentials that fetch a short-lived token in `preAuthentication` (for example the GitHub App API credential, whose installation token expires after one hour) ar
e refreshed in `requestWithAuthentication` only in the `catch` block, by calling `credentialsHelper.preAuthentication(..., true)` after a thrown error (`packages
/core/src/execution-engine/node-execution-context/utils/request-helpers/authentication.ts`).

The HTTP Request node sets `requestOptions.simple = false` when "Never Error" is on (`HttpRequestV3.node.ts`). Then a 401 does not throw, it resolves as a respon
se, so the `catch` block never runs. The expired token stays in the credential, and every request with "Never Error" returns the 401 to the workflow as data unti
l a different request without "Never Error" throws a 401 and triggers the refresh.

This is easy to hit in scheduled workflows. A run every 30 or 60 minutes can refresh the token at the start of one run, and the token then expires during a later
 run.

The OAuth2 path already handles this case: `requestOAuth2` turns a resolved 401 under `simple: false` into its refresh path (`retryWithNewToken` in `request-help
ers/oauth.ts`, see the comment "resolves with the original response under `simple: false` instead of throwing"). The `preAuthentication` path has no equivalent.

`httpRequestWithAuthentication` has the same shape: it refreshes only in its `catch`, based on `error.response?.status`, so with `ignoreHttpStatusErrors` it shou
ld have the same gap. I read this in the code but did not run it.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a GitHub App API credential.
2. Add an HTTP Request node: GET `https://api.github.com/installation/repositories`, with "Never Error" and "Include Response Headers and Status" on.
3. Run the node. Wait more than one hour and run it again.
4. The node returns `statusCode: 401` with "Bad credentials". The credential is not refreshed, so every following run returns 401 as well.

### Expected behavior

A 401 for a credential with an expiring token starts one refresh and one resend of the request, with or without "Never Error", as it does without it today. Other
 statuses keep the current behavior: with "Never Error" they are valid results for the workflow and must not be resent.

A request whose body was consumed (stream or multipart) cannot be sent again. The existing `catch` path already skips the resend in that case, and the same shoul
d hold here.

### Proposed fix

I have a tested change for `requestWithAuthentication`: read the status of a `simple: false` response, request the full response for the first attempt, return on
ly the body when the caller did not ask for the full response, and refresh and resend once on a 401 only. It comes with 7 new tests that fail without the change.
 I opened it as #43834, which was closed automatically because `packages/core` and the HTTP Request node are maintained by the team. The diff is there for reuse
if it helps.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
Spot on diagnosis. The discrepancy between `requestOAuth2` (which explicitly handles resolved 401s under `simple: false`) and `requestWithAuthentication` (which strictly encapsulates `credentialsHelper.preAuthentication` in `catch`) is definitely an oversight in the execution engine.

If you already have a working patch mirroring the `oauth.ts` retry pattern, please open a PR against `master` and link it to Linear ticket `GHC-9757`.

In the meantime, handling the failure via the node's generic **Settings > On Error > Continue Regular Output** rather than the HTTP-level "Never Error" (`simple: false`) lets the underlying client throw, hit the `catch` block to refresh the token, and keep your workflow running.
